CancelStatement.name: CancelStatement
CancelStatement.doc: Cancels a running query. To be canceled, a query must be running. For more information about the Amazon Redshift Data API and CLI usage examples, see Using the Amazon Redshift Data API in the Amazon Redshift Management Guide.

DescribeStatement.name: DescribeStatement
DescribeStatement.doc: Describes the details about a specific instance when a query was run by the Amazon Redshift Data API. The information includes when the query started, when it finished, the query status, the number of rows returned, and the SQL statement. For more information about the Amazon Redshift Data API and CLI usage examples, see Using the Amazon Redshift Data API in the Amazon Redshift Management Guide.

SessionTtl.doc: The date and time (UTC) when the session is set to expire and be closed.

CurrentStatementId.doc: The identifier of the SQL statement currently running in the session. This value is a universally unique identifier (UUID) generated by Amazon Redshift Data API. This element is returned only when the session status is BUSY.

SessionData.doc: Contains the metadata for a session returned by ListSessions, including its status, compute target, database connection, and lifecycle timestamps.

value.doc: The value of the parameter. Amazon Redshift implicitly converts to the proper data type. For more information, see Data types in the Amazon Redshift Database Developer Guide.

SqlParameter.doc: A parameter used in a SQL statement.

Id.doc: The SQL statement identifier. This value is a universally unique identifier (UUID) generated by Amazon Redshift Data API.

QueryStrings.doc: One or more SQL statements. Each query string in the array corresponds to one of the queries in a batch query request.

SecretArn.doc: The name or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the secret that enables access to the database.

Status.doc: The status of the SQL statement. An example is the that the SQL statement finished.

StatementName.doc: The name of the SQL statement.

CreatedAt.doc: The date and time (UTC) the statement was created.

UpdatedAt.doc: The date and time (UTC) that the statement metadata was last updated.

QueryParameters.doc: The parameters used in a SQL statement.

IsBatchStatement.doc: A value that indicates whether the statement is a batch query request.

ResultFormat.doc: The data format of the result of the SQL statement.

SessionId.doc: The session identifier of the query.

Id.doc: The identifier of the SQL statement. This value is a universally unique identifier (UUID) generated by Amazon Redshift Data API. A suffix indicates the number of the SQL statement. For example, d9b6c0c9-0747-4bf4-b142-e8883122f766:2 has a suffix of :2 that indicates the second SQL statement of a batch query.

Duration.doc: The amount of time in nanoseconds that the statement ran.

Error.doc: The error message from the cluster if the SQL statement encountered an error while running.

Status.doc: The status of the SQL statement. An example is the that the SQL statement finished.

CreatedAt.doc: The date and time (UTC) the statement was created.

UpdatedAt.doc: The date and time (UTC) that the statement metadata was last updated.

ResultRows.doc: Either the number of rows returned from the SQL statement or the number of rows affected. If result size is greater than zero, the result rows can be the number of rows affected by SQL statements such as INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, COPY, and others. A -1 indicates the value is null.

ResultSize.doc: The size in bytes of the returned results. A -1 indicates the value is null.

RedshiftQueryId.doc: The SQL statement identifier. This value is a universally unique identifier (UUID) generated by Amazon Redshift Data API.

HasResultSet.doc: A value that indicates whether the statement has a result set. The result set can be empty. The value is true for an empty result set.

type.doc: The type of the table. Possible values include TABLE, VIEW, SYSTEM TABLE, GLOBAL TEMPORARY, LOCAL TEMPORARY, ALIAS, and SYNONYM.
